findings.claim: The dead-end trigger for the blocked writer cannot be proven on a v9 birth as the plan defines v9. The design takes the remediation ceiling, replan_required and graph_integrity from the general Executor and Decision_Policy text. It does not check that v9's native roster can produce any of them. The plan says v9 'keeps every v8 method ID, and adds two writers'. v8's native chain has no retry, repair, failed-result or step-block writer. So the input 'authentic owner block record' (design §2.4 input 3b) has no source, and W-B would be installed but never able to write. Cards B-1 and B-3 promise that 'the run history shows real dead ends' and that stalled runs 'can be aborted as soon as v9 exists'. The depth forecast gives `producer` a PASS. All of these rest on the gap.
findings.verified_evidence: A1 native-v8 protocol.md @e8d61ace4 line 129: 'Unsupported retry, general repair, waiver, exception, child or unknown writer branches remain unadmitted'. Line 163 (begin_attempt): 'Its WorkNode is queued, has no prior attempt, empty retries…'. Line 165: 'terminal_result, result_ref and blocked_state_ref are null'. Line 169 (record_verified): 'Failing/blocked/skipped/unresolved results cannot use this method.' native-v8/methods.json @A1 lists 18 methods: admit_first_attempt, capture_original_input, begin_attempt, submit_verification, record_verified, complete_worknode, publish_execution, publish_provisional_success, issue_final_decision, capture_standard.v2, prepare_certified, publish_certified_joint, read_retained, read_standard, update_execution, update_provisional, update_certified, read_current. None of them records a failure, a block episode or a retry. B2 F9 already says 'a v8 run has no blocked path at all'. The design does not carry this into v9. With no second attempt, a 3-generation remediation ceiling (Decision_Policy 423) cannot be reached.
findings.suggested_repair: Re-derive B-1's options against the native roster v9 actually installs. For example, the real v9 dead end may be a first attempt whose non-pass result no installed writer can record, before Replan release. Otherwise add native outcome writers to v9's scope, as a stated scope and product change shown on the card. Say which on cards B-1 and B-3, in the plan's §2 and §3, and in the design's §2.3. Add an owner question to TB-02, and to T-02/TB-03: does an unrecordable failed attempt leave the run permanently not quiet? That would also leave a C-3 stop pending forever. Label the import of Executor and Decision_Policy causes 'by analogy' until this is settled.

findings.section: §2.3 option table and trigger item 2; §7.2 card B-1 (option 1, Recommendation); §7.4 card B-3 (What it costs, option 1)
findings.claim: Option 1 is defined as a step 'stuck on something only Replan or Abort can clear', and the card says it 'breaks no button'. Canon names other exits for two of the three causes: a manual fix, or a patch. A recorded blocked run is fenced (GRS 3468), so option 1 would remove those exits and the step buttons for the recorded run. B-3's 'Under B-1 option 1 such a run could not have continued anyway' is false by the same text. graph_integrity is a failure class ('hard fail'), not a blocked reason code, so reading it as a block is an unlabelled inference. The card lists 'the final check fails on an open blocker' without condition, but design §2.3 and §2.4 admit it only if TB-12 creates a non-pass record.
findings.verified_evidence: Decision_Policy.md @63cf2cb line 423: '`remediation_ceiling_exceeded` | no automatic retry | … | remain blocked until replan, manual fix, or abort'. Executor_Protocol.md @63cf2cb line 419: '`replan_required` | 0 | — | No | remain blocked until patch or replan is applied'. Line 418: '`failure_class` | `graph_integrity` | 0 | — | No | hard fail; replan path only'. GRS 3468: '`blocked` and `stopped` are fenced, resumable only through a new revision and valid `goal_run.replanned` admission.' UCC 1156-1167 and 8148 list the step actions (retry_now, start_fresh_attempt, resume_after_prerequisite, skip_node, replan, abort_run). B2 §3 rows T10 and T11 quote the same lines, yet summarise them as 'only Replan clears it'.
findings.suggested_repair: Correct §2.3 and cards B-1 and B-3 before they are shown. Say that canon also names 'manual fix' (DP 423) and 'patch' (EP 419) as exits, and that option 1 removes them once a run is recorded blocked. State the button effect honestly. Mark the graph_integrity mapping as an inference and add it as an owner question. Make the G4 cause conditional on TB-12 in the card text too.

findings.section: Design §0 'Two landings', §4.1, §4.3, §9 step 1; plan §0 item 2, §4.1 'Source', §9 steps 3-5, Q-V9-08; addendum §4.1 'Timing', §4.2 census
findings.claim: The three notes disagree on where the A3 source contracts (landing 1) land. The design assumes they sit inside the v9 package and its canon landing (V1-Q8, 'This design assumes that'). The plan and the addendum have them land before v9, so that v9 pins their landed bytes. The census tables follow different orders: the design gives '339 + x' at the v9 landing, the addendum gives 334 at stopped landing 1, and the plan gives 338 to 339 before v9.
findings.verified_evidence: Design §4.1: 'V1 §8 recommends that the v9 profile and the two A3 source contracts share one package and one review round (V1-Q8). This design assumes that.' Plan §0 item 2: 'The stop and blocked source contracts land first, as A3 landing 1 for each. v9 then pins their landed bytes as members'. Plan Q-V9-08 recommends landing before v9. Addendum §4.1: 'Landing 1 lands before the v9 package freezes'.
findings.suggested_repair: Settle Q-V9-08 / V1-Q8 once. Rewrite design §0, §4.1, §4.3 and §9, or the plan and the addendum, to one order. Re-derive one census table from that order.

findings.section: Design §6.2 last bullet, §7.1 card 'The change (exact)', P-01; plan §9 'Two rows in one landing', Q-V9-06; addendum §4.2
findings.claim: Moving two Event registry rows in one joint landing 2 is recommended as a default, but the process text points to one landing per row. Q-02 says 'each landing is answered on its own line', and DL-078's procedure (applied in DL-094) is 'one family per landing'. Q-09 also says to land stopped first. The notes also disagree on which SHA pair each card carries. The design and the card draft use main → whole landing for both cards. The plan uses X→Y for the first row and Y→Z for the second, with Y never on main.
findings.verified_evidence: PA process-answers-20260925.md @616f12bf line 7: 'Cards for two families prepared together may be presented in one batch, but each landing is answered on its own line'. Line 17: 'land `goal_run.stopped` first so the blocked card does not hold up the other work'. DL-078 @63cf2cb (Decision_Log 1571): 'its own Storage admission landing with one family per landing'. Design §6.2: 'both cards show the registry SHA before (main) and after (whole landing) (P-01)'. Plan §9: 'Card for the first row: registry SHA X → Y. Card for the second: Y → Z.'
findings.suggested_repair: Send 'joint landing or two landings' and 'which SHA pair each card shows' to the process thread as one question, citing Q-02 line 7, Q-09 line 17 and DL-078. Record it as open (P-01 = Q-V9-06), not as a recommended default. Align the design, the plan and the addendum on one answer. Keep separate sequential landings as the stated fallback.

findings.claim: The plan recommends that the v9 freeze wait for B-1. That makes the live stop writer and stopped's landing 2 wait on the blocked card. It cites only C-4 and does not mention Q-09's instruction that the blocked card must not hold up stopped. The design records the tension (P-03). The plan settles it by recommendation.
findings.verified_evidence: PA line 17 (Q-09): 'land `goal_run.stopped` first so the blocked card does not hold up the other work'. Cards file line 117 (C-4): 'one v9 carries both the stop and the blocked writers once blocked's trigger is decided'. Design P-03: 'Q-09 says stopped must not wait on the blocked card'.
findings.suggested_repair: Cite Q-09 in §6.1. Present 'wait' against 'v9 stop-only plus v10 blocked' as a tension between C-4 and Q-09, for Jared or the process thread to decide, with no recommendation. Or recommend only presenting B-1 now, as the design does.

findings.section: §6.3 option (a); §8 table row v8 ('v8 births only under RR-1 or RR-3') and §8 lead ('Rules R1 to R4 … hold: linear')
findings.claim: The plan says the one chain is linear under R1. It still lists options that need a second per-run projector (RR-1, and §6.3 (a) 'two projectors') without saying that they break R1 and DL-080's single mandatory projection.
findings.verified_evidence: A2 R2-projection.md §4.4, RR-1: 'Two per-run projectors derive replanned rows. Breaks R1.' Stopped design line 298, R1: 'There is no second projector for the per-run role.' Plan §6.3 (a): 'v9 carries the forked type unchanged (RR-1 again, two projectors)'.
findings.suggested_repair: Mark option (a) and every RR-1 branch in §8 as breaking R1, needing an explicit exception against DL-080. Or drop them from the chain table.

findings.section: §2.4 input 6 (allowed actions); §3 payload table row allowed_action_ids
findings.claim: The design says the first contract's action set is 'exactly ["stop_goal"]'. It only argues against retry-type ActionIds. Seven other ActionIds get no reason: narrow_scope, request_approval, change_model, change_account, restore_from_mandatory_backup, abandon_preserved_work and resolve_owner_conflict. 'cannot be owner-valid' is an inference stated as fact. D-R16 also ties permission and recovery branches to D-R01, which the design does not read.
findings.verified_evidence: GRS @63cf2cb line 3502: ActionId = retry_same_action, replan, narrow_scope, request_approval, change_model, change_account, retry_storage, restore_from_mandatory_backup, abandon_preserved_work, resolve_owner_conflict, cancel_goal, stop_goal, resume_after_revalidation. Line 3732: 'allowed actions are non-empty and owner-valid; permission/recovery branches carry the same restrictions as `D-R01`.'
findings.suggested_repair: Give a one-line reason for each of the 13 ActionIds: no bound issuer in v9, fenced by GRS 3468, or needs D06. Label the reasons as inference. Read D-R01 for the permission and recovery branches. Keep TB-07 and TB-22 open until an owner confirms.

findings.claim: Jared's approved C-2 option says Abort is stopped and not resumable. The addendum gives both commands resumable=false. Under D-R21 that still allows a resume through a distinct replan. It then turns 'whether Abort needs a stronger bar' into a new open question for A3-replanned. The approved rule is not carried into the stopped contract.
findings.verified_evidence: Cards file C-2 option 1, approved: 'Pause is stopped and resumable later through replan. Abort is stopped and not resumable.' GRS @63cf2cb line 3767: '`resumable=false` forbids future resume without a distinct replan that proves changed admission conditions.'
findings.suggested_repair: Have the stopped GRS unit state C-2's rule as a binding constraint on the later replanned contract: an Abort-origin stop is not resumable. Reword T-25 to ask how to enforce it, for example refusing a replan whose stop intent came from abort_run, not whether.

findings.section: Design §4.2 (landing 2 rows), §7.1 card ('The only other row this landing changes is #/families/5'); plan §7 'Certified for v9 births'

findings.claim: None of the three notes edits the independent validator or reseals governance. No blocked trigger, writer input or exit depends on D06. The projection chain v5 → v6 → v7 (stopped + blocked) → v8 (replanned) is linear and follows DL-080's order. The v9 carry-forward drops no v8 method.

The validator lives at Plans/.audits/event-authority-2026-08-12/independent-validator/pm_event_authority_independent_validator.py; its lines 269, 294 and 623-626 match the design.
